content:
In this sustained benchmark with a “typical” BPMN process (10 service tasks, 200 ms each, 2 timers of 1 minute), TaktX demonstrated both high throughput and stable latency at scale. With one engine node, throughput plateaued around 850 PI/s (~12k flow nodes/s) while sustaining 100k+ concurrent active processes with sub-second latency (p95 ~400–500 ms). With two engine nodes, throughput scaled nearly linearly to ~1,700 PI/s (~24k flow nodes/s) with 200k+ concurrent processes — without any meaningful increase in latency. Process durations tracked the theoretical 122 s baseline, confirming timers and workers were correctly orchestrated under load.

Beyond raw performance, these results translate directly into cost eﬃciency. Achieving this level of throughput on just 2×4-vCPU engine nodes (plus a small 3-broker cluster) means materially fewer cores and fewer machines to reach a given PI/s target, no heavyweight scale-up RDBMS tier acting as a bottleneck, and therefore lower cloud spend (compute and storage), simpler operations, and a smaller energy footprint. In practical terms, teams can meet or raise SLAs with far less hardware, cutting recurring infrastructure costs while keeping latency predictable.

TaktX is not only capable of extreme raw throughput (Scenario 1) but also delivers real-world, sustained performance with linear scalability — turning high-volume automation into a performance-per-euro advantage.
